problem: If $|u\cdot v|+‖u+v‖=34$ and $‖v‖=6$, then what is the smallest possible value of $‖u‖?$
worked_solution:
First, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, simplifying, and substituting in the given information, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}34 & =|u\cdot v|+‖u+v‖ \\  & \le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖+‖u+v‖ \\  & =‖u‖\cdot (6)+‖u+v‖ \\  & =6‖u‖+‖u+v‖.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, using the triangle inequality, simplifying, and substituting in the given information, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}6‖u‖+‖u+v‖ & \le 6‖u‖+(‖u‖+‖v‖) \\  & =6‖u‖+(‖u‖+6) \\  & =7‖u‖+6.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining the two inequalities, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}34 & \le 7‖u‖+6 \\ 28 & \le 7‖u‖ \\ 4 & \le ‖u‖.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $‖u‖$ is $4.$
